newsitem.title: UK: Labour lodges complaint over Stagecoach.
newsitem.headline: Labour lodges complaint over Stagecoach.

text.p: Britain's main opposition Labour party accused Stagecoach Holdings Plc on Monday of failing to deliver the improved service it promised a year ago when it was awarded the privatisation franchise for South West Trains.
Labour's transport spokesman, Andrew Smith, said he had written to the government's rail franchising director demanding immediate action to bring forward the promised improvements.
"I have called also for assurances that these broken privatisation promises are not repeated on other lines," Smith said in a statement.
Labour published an analysis that it said showed South West Trains had clearly delivered only two of the 13 improvements it undertook to make within the first year of its franchise.

"South West Trains (SWT) have broken their privatisation pledges, leaving passengers cheated of the travel information and rail services they were promised a year ago. This nails the lie that privatisation is a cure-all for the Tories' transport chaos," Smith said.

The attack by Labour, which has vowed tighter rail regulation if it wins the coming election, coincides with the introduction on Monday by SWT of an emergency timetable to tackle problems caused by driver shortages.
The company expects to cancel some 250 services this week following a productivity deal reached with its 750 drivers for 70 to take voluntary redundancy.
SWT said it had underestimated the impact of taking drivers off duty for training on the new routes they would be driving.

The rail franchising office has approved SWT's application to introduce a special timetable, which it said would allow the company to make timetable adjustments that would eventually benefit customers.
Stagecoach could face heavy penalties by the government's rail franchising authorities over the cancellations.
SWT, which operates rail services from London to Southampton, Weymouth and Exeter, said the cancellations would help it produce a more reliable, although reduced timetable.
